Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral pneumothoraces (visible pleural lines with absent lung markings peripherally) and a distinct radiolucent halo surrounding the cardiac silhouette, indicative of pneumopericardium. This combination is classically associated with the erosion of a cavitating lesion (such as invasive aspergillosis) into the pericardial space, leading to tension pneumopericardium and subsequent cardiac arrest.
